subject: General Science
title: Chemical Bonding

outcomes.text: illustrate chemical bonding in common compounds,
identify bond types in common compounds,
distinguish structures of selected elements and compounds,
describe the relationship between the bond types and the physical properties of elements and compounds,
select appropriate materials for use based on their bond type and structure,
reflect on the appropriateness of substances used in day-to-day life.

content: Bond formation in common compounds and metals
Uses of Diamond, Graphite and Aluminium.
inquiry_questions: How do bond types relate to physical properties of compounds?
suggested_learning_experiences: Discuss with peers the role of valence electrons in bond formation.
Search for information from online or other available resources on the bond types of common compounds (water, sodium chloride, hydrogen gas, oxygen gas, iodine, Diamond and Graphite).
Navigate through online sources to access virtual laboratories for simulations on formation of chemical bonds.
Discuss with peers the formation of different types of chemical bonds (ionic, covalent, dative-covalent, hydrogen, metallic and Van der Waals).
Use dots (•) and crosses (x) to illustrate chemical bonding for selected molecules and compounds.
Observe safety precautions when carrying out activities to investigate properties of elements and compounds.
Carry out activities to demonstrate physical properties of different elements and compounds (melting point, boiling point, solubility, electrical and thermal conductivity).
Discuss with peers the relationship between bond types and physical properties of different structures (giant ionic, simple molecular, giant atomic and giant metallic).
Explore with peers the uses of elements and compounds based on their bond types and structures (diamond, graphite and Aluminium).
Project: Model structures of molecules and compounds using locally available resources.
Project: Sensitise the community on use and care of common appliances such as utensils and other cookware (Aluminium).
coreCompetencies:
Communication and collaboration: as the learner sensitises the community on use and care of common appliances such as utensils and other cookware.
Digital literacy: the learner navigates through online sources to access virtual laboratories for simulations on formation of chemical bonds.
Creativity and imagination: as the learner undertakes a project of modelling ball and stick ionic and covalent structures of selected molecules using locally available resources.
values:
Respect: as the learner recognises and appreciates the input of every group member when discussing the relationship between bond types and physical properties of different structures.
Patriotism: as the learner sensitises the community on use and care of common appliances such as utensils and other cookware.
pcis:
Safety and Security: as the learner observes safety precautions when carrying out activities to investigate properties of elements and compounds.
Financial Literacy: as the learner makes informed decisions when selecting appropriate items, appliances and equipment made from specific elements and compounds.

The source lists diverse substances and property tests. Any heating, flame, gas, acid, electrical or chemical handling requires local approval, appropriate equipment and risk assessment; use models, reference data or teacher-controlled demonstration where a learner practical would be unsafe.
Bond type, particle structure and bulk properties must be distinguished accurately; model diagrams do not establish that a material was physically tested.
